summary: The Fed path is still the top risk: October core CPI +0.3% (third straight) has a December hike fully priced with some 50bp odds, and the 10Y is back at 5.07%. AI and chip policy risk jumped after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12 amid a probe with a China-intelligence angle and a reported export-control review. Iran risk tilts back up after Trump posted that the US does not need a deal.

risks.title: Fed hiking path and Fed leadership (Chair Warsh)
risks.status: Held 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 (Hammack and Cook dissented for a hike); October CPI +0.4% / core +0.3% m/m vs +0.3% / +0.2% (third straight 0.3% core; shelter +0.3%); Waller had set ~0.3% core as the bar for considering 50bp; Logan wants 'at least two more' hikes; Nov 12 claims 200K (prior 191K); Hammack, Williams, Barr, Daly speak Nov 12; PPI Nov 13; November CPI lands after the Dec 9 decision
risks.odds: Dec 9 hike 100%, implied 4.17% (+29bp) (fed funds futures, Nov 12); FedWatch after CPI about 88.5-89.8% 25bp / 10.2-11.5% 50bp (sources conflict, Nov 10-11)
risks.impact: A hot PPI or 50bp signal pushes the 10Y toward 5.31% and hits long-duration tech, small caps and housing; a soft PPI and a 25bp-and-pause message would ease yields and help rate-sensitive groups

risks.title: AI / chip policy: Nvidia leadership crisis, export controls and data-center backlash
risks.status: Nov 12 (8:48 ET): Nvidia said Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and director effective immediately after a board probe of reported affairs (one with a woman US reports link to Chinese intelligence); CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, Harvey Jones the first board chair, a CEO search is under way; Q3 results still Nov 17. NVDA opened about -14%, pared to about -7%. Earlier: The Information reported $7.5B of Nvidia hardware reached China via a Huang-linked network; the White House is reportedly weighing new export controls on advanced Nvidia chips; post-midterm data-center moratorium pledges (Texas). CoreWeave beat Q3 and raised guidance (backlog $132.5B) but fell 9-13% today; Nebius -19%
risks.market_pricing: Nov 12: SMH -2.35% (-10.7pp vs SPY over 1 month), XLK -1.29%; VIX only +4% to 18.2
risks.impact: Formal export controls, a messy succession or a weak Nov 17 report would extend the AI de-rating and drag cap-weighted indexes; a clean Nov 17 report with intact guidance would show the business is separate from the governance issue and spark a short-covering rally

risks.title: US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz closure
risks.status: Nov 12 (8:15 ET): Trump posted 'We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed', claimed the US holds Iran's money and 'their Strait', and told Vance to focus on crime in Democratic-run states, a day after the WSJ said Vance was weighing direct talks with Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei (Rezaei denies talks). Strikes have largely subsided into a stalemate; Qatar-led mediation and a Qatari-Pakistani reopening plan had been gaining momentum; the interim deal is unsigned and the blockade remains
risks.odds: US-Iran ceasefire holds to Dec 31: 25% (Polymarket via ScanX, early Nov); no fresh reading found
risks.market_pricing: Nov 12: Brent 93.76 (+1.08%), WTI 86.76 (+0.27%) after the post; Brent -11.6% over 1 month; XLE +0.85% (leading)
risks.impact: A collapse of diplomacy or renewed strikes would send Brent back above $100-110 and add to inflation and hike pricing; a signed deal reopening Hormuz would push Brent toward the low $80s and help consumers, transports and rate-sensitive stocks while hurting energy and defense

risks.title: China-Taiwan tensions and chip export controls / tariffs
risks.status: The White House is reportedly considering new export controls on Nvidia's advanced chips (Nov 10, not officially confirmed); the Huang resignation has a China-intelligence angle that raises the odds of congressional scrutiny of chip-China ties; Taiwan curbed short selling and readied a stabilization fund on Nov 9; Chinese live-fire drills in mid-October; a report says US tariffs on Chinese chips are delayed to June 2027 (unconfirmed)
risks.market_pricing: SMH -15.8% over 3 months (-13.5pp vs SPY); SOXX 30% below its 52-week high
risks.impact: New export curbs or a Taiwan blockade drill would hit semis first; a trade thaw or no new rules after the Nvidia exit would help a rebound

risks.title: US government funding / shutdown risk
risks.status: The stopgap signed in early September funds the government through Dec 11; the House has passed 3 of 12 FY2027 bills (all 12 cleared committee) while Senate appropriations are deadlocked; the fight moves to a lame-duck session before the new Democratic Congress; no November deal reported
risks.impact: A December lapse would delay economic data (including releases the Fed needs) and dent Q4 growth; a full-year deal or a clean CR into the new Congress removes it

risks.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping
risks.status: A Houthi attack reportedly damaged Aramco offices in Riyadh (reported Nov 9, not confirmed elsewhere); Saudi-coalition operations against the Houthis; Saudi Arabia warned its Yanbu Red Sea oil hub could be targeted (Nov 6); no new incident found Nov 11-12
risks.market_pricing: No visible Red Sea premium shift; Brent moves are driven by Iran headlines
risks.impact: A hit on Saudi export infrastructure (Yanbu, the Red Sea alternative to Hormuz) would be a major oil shock; calm keeps the focus on Iran diplomacy

risks.title: OPEC+ output policy
risks.status: Nov 1: OPEC+ kept output targets unchanged through December; next meeting Nov 29; Goldman's December Brent forecast is $105 (2027 average $88)
risks.market_pricing: Brent 93.76, well below Goldman's $105 December forecast
risks.impact: A surprise increase would be bearish for oil and energy stocks; continued restraint keeps a floor under oil if an Iran deal reopens supply

risks.title: Israel government formation after the Oct 27 election
risks.status: Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot the mandate on Nov 8 after 67 recommendations vs 46 for Netanyahu; Eisenkot has 28 days (extendable by 14) and says he is open to including Netanyahu; Arab-led parties back him from outside; Netanyahu stays caretaker PM and pushes for a unity government
risks.impact: An Eisenkot-led or unity government would likely be more cautious on Iran and Gaza (mildly bearish oil and defense); a failed mandate or a new election extends caretaker uncertainty

risks.title: Russia-Ukraine war and peace talks
risks.status: US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11), the first trilateral round since February, focused on security guarantees; Russia sent a higher-level delegation; no outcome reported yet; local truce in one town since Oct 27
risks.odds: Peace talks by Dec 31 90%, ceasefire by Dec 31 9.5%, by Mar 31 2027 23.5% (Polymarket via Rio Times, early Nov)
risks.impact: Real progress would be mildly bearish for defense and European gas; a collapse keeps the defense theme supported

risks.title: US midterm elections: divided government
risks.status: Resolved Nov 3-4: Democrats won the House and Senate; the new Congress sits in January; Republicans including Vance blame the Iran war for the losses; Trump is now redirecting Vance to domestic issues
risks.odds: Resolved (pre-vote: Democrats Senate 73%, prediction markets via Yahoo Finance Nov 3)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 4: Dow ~+2%, S&P +1.1%; homebuilders +6.4%, defense lower
risks.impact: Gridlock limits new fiscal policy; oversight of tariffs, defense, AI and the Iran war rises; the risk is now in specific sectors rather than the index
